title: Hire to Retire: Phantom Payroll: Untangling Off-Cycle Payments and Cost-Center Chaos at Meridian Craft Foods
context: Meridian Craft Foods is a fictional mid-sized specialty food manufacturer with 2,400 employees across three plants and a head office. Over the past 18 months the company grew rapidly through seasonal hiring and two small acquisitions. HR onboarding is handled in a legacy applicant-tracking spreadsheet, while payroll runs in the ERP's HCM/payroll module. Position data, cost-center assignments, and termination records are maintained manually by plant HR coordinators and re-keyed by the central payroll team. Finance has begun monthly labor-cost reviews ahead of a planned refinancing, and the CFO has asked for a rapid diagnostic of why payroll-related costs and corrections keep climbing despite stable headcount.
challenge: Diagnose why Meridian's payroll costs, off-cycle payment volume, and labor-cost reporting errors are rising despite flat headcount, and recommend a practical, ERP-enabled Hire to Retire improvement that Finance and HR can implement within two quarters.
symptoms: Off-cycle (manual) payroll payments have risen from ~15 to over 110 per month in a year, each requiring manual approval and bank file handling.
Monthly labor-cost reports show 6-9% of payroll expense posted to a default 'suspense' cost center, forcing Finance to reallocate manually at close.
Internal audit found 14 terminated employees who received at least one paycheck after their separation date in the last two quarters.
New-hire first paychecks are late or wrong for roughly 1 in 5 seasonal hires, driving HR hotline volume and some early attrition.
Month-end close for payroll-related accounts now takes 6 business days, up from 3, due to reconciliation and reclassification work.

evidence.finding: Off-cycle payment reasons: 48% 'new hire not in payroll system at cutoff', 27% 'retro pay for late data entry', 15% 'termination processed after pay run', 10% other. Average 11 calendar days between a plant HR action and its entry in the ERP payroll module.

Suspense postings concentrate in the two acquired plants, whose employees were loaded with placeholder cost centers during migration; 1,180 of 2,400 employee master records have no validated position-to-cost-center mapping in the ERP org structure.

Terminations are initiated on paper forms signed by plant supervisors; median elapsed time from last working day to payroll-effective termination in the ERP is 9 days. Overpayments to 14 separated employees total $41,300, of which $12,800 is deemed unrecoverable.

Tickets tagged 'pay incorrect/missing' grew 170% year over year; 62% of these tickets originate from employees hired within the prior 60 days, and resolution requires an average of 3 handoffs between plant HR, central HR, and payroll.

evidence.source: ERP Access and Workflow Configuration Review
evidence.finding: The ERP's hire, transfer, and termination workflow capabilities are licensed but not activated; all employee master changes are entered centrally by two payroll clerks from emailed spreadsheets, with no automated validation of cost center, position, or effective dates.

participant_deliverable: A 5-minute team presentation stating the root-cause diagnosis, a phased ERP-enabled remediation plan for the Hire to Retire process (people, process, and system actions), 3-4 measurable success targets, and the top risks with mitigations.

agenda.activity: Facilitator introduces the case, objectives, and deliverable expectations
Teams read the brief and evidence pack; clarifying questions to facilitator
Team working session: root-cause diagnosis and ERP-enabled solution design
Teams finalize success measures, risks, and build the 5-minute presentation
Team presentations with facilitator challenge questions
Debrief: facilitator shares model diagnosis and key Hire to Retire lessons
